unitTitle: The Imperative - Reflexive Pronouns - Might/Could - Must/Have to - Can/Be allowed to - Could/Couldn't

pairsWith.noteUz: Bu nazariya beti Coursebook 10-unit (Stick to the Rules!) grammatikasini takrorlaydi: buyruq mayli, o'zlik olmoshlari, modal fe'llar.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 10-UNIT NAZARIYA (50-bet, PDF 49). Yuqorida chapda ko'k '10', sarlavha: 'The Imperative - Reflexive Pronouns - Might/Could - Must/Have to - Can/Be allowed to - Could/Couldn't'. Och pushti ramka, ikki ustun.

CHAP USTUN:
'The Imperative': • The imperative is formed with the verb without a subject. 'Open the door!' The negative imperative is formed with do not/don't and the verb. 'Don't touch that!' The imperative refers to the second person singular and plural. • We use the imperative to: - give orders: 'Write your name here.' - give instructions: 'Take a deep breath.' - offer something: 'Have some tea.' - make a request: 'Be quiet, please.' Note: We usually add the word please at the beginning or at the end of the sentence.
'Reflexive Pronouns': JADVAL Subject pronouns / Reflexive pronouns: I - myself; you - yourself; he - himself; she - herself; it - itself; we - ourselves; you - yourselves; they - themselves. We use reflexive pronouns: • with verbs such as behave, burn, cut, enjoy, hurt, introduce, kill, look at, teach, etc when the subject and the object of the verb refer to the same person. 'Harry (subject) has cut himself (object).'
'Might/Could': We use might/could to express possibility. '"Where's Sarah?" "She might/could be at the beach." (Perhaps she's at the beach.)'

O'NG USTUN:
'Must - Have to': • We use must and have to to express obligation and necessity. 'You must stay in bed. I have to go to the post office.' • Must can only be used in the present tense. We use have to to form all the other tenses. 'I'll have to work on Saturday. She had to stay in bed.' • We use must/mustn't to give strong advice. 'You must see a doctor right away. You mustn't eat too many sweets.' • We also use mustn't to express prohibition. 'You mustn't park here. (= You aren't allowed to park here; it's against the rules.)' • We use don't/doesn't have to to express lack of necessity. 'You don't have to buy any oranges. We've got plenty.' • The past forms of have to and don't have to are had to and didn't have to. 'When I was your age I had to walk to school! We didn't have to learn a foreign language when we were students.'
'Can - Be allowed to': • We use can to ask for or give permission and can't to refuse permission. '"Can I watch TV?" "Of course, you can." I'm afraid you can't take pictures.' • We use be allowed to to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker. 'Am I allowed to park my motorcycle here? (What is the law?) You aren't allowed to take photographs in the museum.'
'Could - Couldn't': • Could and couldn't are the past forms of can and can't. 'I could go to bed late when I was 17 but I couldn't drink wine.'

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '50'.

exercises.instructionEn: The imperative is formed with the verb without a subject: Open the door! The negative imperative is formed with do not/don't and the verb: Don't touch that! The imperative refers to the second person singular and plural. We use the imperative to give orders (Write your name here), give instructions (Take a deep breath), offer something (Have some tea), make a request (Be quiet, please). Note: We usually add the word please at the beginning or at the end of the sentence.
exercises.instructionUz: Buyruq mayli fe'lning egasiz shakli bilan yasaladi: Eshikni och! Inkor buyruq do not/don't + fe'l: Unga tegma! Buyruq mayli 2-shaxs birlik va ko'plikka qaratiladi. Buyruq mayli: buyruq berish (Ismingizni shu yerga yozing), ko'rsatma berish (Chuqur nafas oling), taklif qilish (Choy iching), iltimos qilish (Jim bo'ling, iltimos) uchun. Eslatma: odatda gap boshida yoki oxirida 'please' qo'shiladi.
exercises.explanationUz:
BUYRUQ MAYLI - EGASIZ FE'L.

  TASDIQ: OPEN the door!
  INKOR:  DON'T TOUCH that!

  Faqat 'you' (sen/siz) ga
  qaratiladi - ega yozilmaydi.


QAChON:

  1) BUYRUQ: Write your name here.
  2) KO'RSATMA: Take a deep
     breath.
  3) TAKLIF: Have some tea.
  4) ILTIMOS: Be quiet, please.

  ⚠ 'please' - boshida yoki
  oxirida: 'Please be quiet.' /
  'Be quiet, please.'


⚠ 'DON'T' HAMMA FE'LGA:

  'Don't be late!' (Don't are ✗).


⚠ 'TO TAKE A DEEP BREATH':

  = chuqur nafas olmoq.

points.en: Open the door! — Don't touch that! (verb without a subject; don't + verb)
points.uz: Eshikni och! — Unga tegma! (egasiz fe'l; don't + fe'l)

points.en: Write your name here. (order) — Take a deep breath. (instruction)
points.uz: Ismingizni shu yerga yozing. (buyruq) — Chuqur nafas oling. (ko'rsatma)

points.en: Have some tea. (offer) — Be quiet, please. (request)

exercises.instructionEn: Reflexive pronouns: I - myself; you - yourself; he - himself; she - herself; it - itself; we - ourselves; you - yourselves; they - themselves. We use reflexive pronouns with verbs such as behave, burn, cut, enjoy, hurt, introduce, kill, look at, teach, etc when the subject and the object of the verb refer to the same person: Harry has cut himself. Might/Could: We use might/could to express possibility: 'Where's Sarah?' 'She might/could be at the beach.' (Perhaps she's at the beach.)
exercises.instructionUz: O'zlik olmoshlari: I - myself; you - yourself; he - himself; she - herself; it - itself; we - ourselves; you - yourselves; they - themselves. O'zlik olmoshlari behave, burn, cut, enjoy, hurt, introduce, kill, look at, teach kabi fe'llar bilan, ega va to'ldiruvchi BIR ShAXS bo'lganda ishlatiladi: Harri o'zini kesib oldi. Might/Could: might/could EHTIMOLni bildiradi: 'Sara qayerda?' 'U plyajda bo'lishi mumkin.' (Balki u plyajda.)
exercises.explanationUz:
O'ZLIK OLMOShLARI - O'ZIM, O'ZING
  ...

  I    → MYSELF     (o'zim)
  you  → YOURSELF   (o'zing)
  he   → HIMSELF    (o'zi - erkak)
  she  → HERSELF    (o'zi - ayol)
  it   → ITSELF     (o'zi - narsa)
  we   → OURSELVES  (o'zimiz)
  you  → YOURSELVES (o'zingiz)
  they → THEMSELVES (o'zlari)

  ⚠ Birlik -SELF, ko'plik -SELVES.
  ⚠ himself (hisself ✗),
    themselves (theirselves ✗).

  QAChON: ega va to'ldiruvchi BIR
  ShAXS:
    Harry has cut HIMSELF. (Harri
    o'zini kesdi)
  Fe'llar: behave, burn, cut,
  enjoy, hurt, introduce, kill,
  look at, teach


MIGHT / COULD - EHTIMOL:

  'Where's Sarah?'
  'She MIGHT / COULD be at the
  beach.' (balki)

  ⚠ might = could = bo'lishi
  mumkin (50%).

exercises.instructionEn: We use must and have to to express obligation and necessity: You must stay in bed. I have to go to the post office. Must can only be used in the present tense. We use have to to form all the other tenses: I'll have to work on Saturday. She had to stay in bed. We use must/mustn't to give strong advice: You must see a doctor right away. You mustn't eat too many sweets. We also use mustn't to express prohibition: You mustn't park here. (= You aren't allowed to park here; it's against the rules.) We use don't/doesn't have to to express lack of necessity: You don't have to buy any oranges. We've got plenty. The past forms of have to and don't have to are had to and didn't have to: When I was your age I had to walk to school! We didn't have to learn a foreign language when we were students.
exercises.instructionUz: Must va have to MAJBURIYAT va ZARURATni bildiradi: Siz yotoqda yotishingiz kerak. Men pochtaga borishim kerak. Must faqat hozirgi zamonda; boshqa zamonlar have to bilan: Shanba kuni ishlashimga to'g'ri keladi. U yotoqda yotishga majbur bo'ldi. Must/mustn't KUChLI MASLAHAT uchun: Darhol shifokorga borishingiz kerak. Ko'p shirinlik yemasligingiz kerak. Mustn't TAQIQ uchun ham: Bu yerda mashina qo'yish mumkin emas. (= qoidaga zid). Don't/doesn't have to ZARURAT YO'QLIGIni bildiradi: Apelsin sotib olishingiz shart emas. Bizda ko'p bor. Have to va don't have to ning o'tgan zamoni - had to va didn't have to: Sening yoshingda men maktabga piyoda borishga majbur edim! Talabaligimizda chet tili o'rganishimiz shart emas edi.
exercises.explanationUz:
MUST / HAVE TO - KERAK, MAJBUR.

  MUST - so'zlovchining fikri /
    kuchli maslahat:
    You MUST stay in bed.
    You MUST see a doctor right
    away.

  HAVE TO - tashqi majburiyat
    (qoida, holat):
    I HAVE TO go to the post
    office.

  ⚠ MUST faqat HOZIRGI zamon.
  Boshqa zamonlar HAVE TO bilan:
    I'LL HAVE TO work on Saturday.
    She HAD TO stay in bed.


INKORLAR - MA'NOSI BUTUNLAY
  BOShQA!

  MUSTN'T = TAQIQ (qilma!):
    You MUSTN'T park here. (qoidaga
    zid)
    You MUSTN'T eat too many
    sweets.

  DON'T HAVE TO = ShART EMAS
    (xohlasang qil):
    You DON'T HAVE TO buy oranges.
    We've got plenty.


O'TGAN ZAMON:

  had to - majbur edim:
    I HAD TO walk to school!
  didn't have to - shart emas edi:
    We DIDN'T HAVE TO learn a
    foreign language.


⚠ 'RIGHT AWAY':

  = darhol.


⚠ 'PLENTY':

  = ko'p, yetarlicha.

points.en: You must stay in bed. I have to go to the post office. (obligation, necessity)
points.uz: Siz yotoqda yotishingiz kerak. Men pochtaga borishim kerak. (majburiyat)

points.en: I'll have to work on Saturday. She had to stay in bed. (must - only present; have to - other tenses)
points.uz: Shanba kuni ishlashimga to'g'ri keladi. U yotoqda yotishga majbur bo'ldi. (boshqa zamonlar - have to)

points.en: You must see a doctor right away. You mustn't eat too many sweets. (strong advice)
points.uz: Darhol shifokorga borishingiz kerak. Ko'p shirinlik yemasligingiz kerak. (kuchli maslahat)

points.en: You mustn't park here. (prohibition = You aren't allowed to)
points.uz: Bu yerda mashina qo'yish mumkin emas. (taqiq)

points.en: You don't have to buy any oranges. We've got plenty. (lack of necessity)
points.uz: Apelsin sotib olishingiz shart emas. Bizda ko'p bor. (zarurat yo'q)

points.en: When I was your age I had to walk to school! We didn't have to learn a foreign language. (past)
points.uz: Sening yoshingda maktabga piyoda borishga majbur edim! Chet tili o'rganishimiz shart emas edi. (o'tgan)

sections.title: Can - Be allowed to / Could - Couldn't
sections.titleUz: Can - Be allowed to / Could - Couldn't

exercises.instructionEn: We use can to ask for or give permission and can't to refuse permission: 'Can I watch TV?' 'Of course, you can.' I'm afraid you can't take pictures. We use be allowed to to ask for, give or refuse permission. The permission, however, does not depend on the speaker: Am I allowed to park my motorcycle here? (What is the law?) You aren't allowed to take photographs in the museum. Could and couldn't are the past forms of can and can't: I could go to bed late when I was 17 but I couldn't drink wine.
exercises.instructionUz: Can - ruxsat so'rash yoki berish, can't - ruxsat bermaslik: 'Televizor ko'rsam bo'ladimi?' 'Albatta.' Afsuski, suratga olish mumkin emas. Be allowed to - ruxsat so'rash, berish yoki bermaslik uchun, lekin ruxsat SO'ZLOVChIGA BOG'LIQ EMAS (qoida, qonun): Bu yerga mototsikl qo'yishga ruxsat bormi? (Qonun nima deydi?) Muzeyda suratga olishga ruxsat yo'q. Could va couldn't - can va can't ning o'tgan zamoni: 17 yoshimda kech yotishim mumkin edi, lekin vino icha olmasdim.
exercises.explanationUz:
RUXSAT - CAN / BE ALLOWED TO.

  CAN - so'zlovchi ruxsat beradi:
    'Can I watch TV?' 'Of course,
    you CAN.'
    I'm afraid you CAN'T take
    pictures.

  BE ALLOWED TO - QOIDA / QONUN
    ruxsat beradi (so'zlovchiga
    bog'liq emas):
    AM I ALLOWED TO park my
    motorcycle here? (qonun nima
    deydi?)
    You AREN'T ALLOWED TO take
    photographs in the museum.


COULD / COULDN'T - O'TGAN ZAMON:

  I COULD go to bed late when I
  was 17 but I COULDN'T drink
  wine.
  (mumkin edi / mumkin emas edi)


⚠ 'TO TAKE PICTURES / PHOTOGRAPHS':

  = suratga olmoq.
